name: Head Nod/Shake Pattern
description: Analyzes head nodding and shaking patterns for natural conversational synchronization — AI often desynchronizes.
mechanism:
This method analyzes head gesture dynamics for deepfake detection:

1. **Head Pose Tracking**: Head orientation (yaw, pitch, roll) is estimated per frame using facial landmark geometry or 3D head model fitting. Head pose signals are decomposed to identify gestural movements (nods = pitch oscillation, shakes = yaw oscillation).

2. **Gesture Kinematics Analysis**: Natural head gestures follow specific kinematics: (a) nodding involves 10-20° pitch oscillation at 1-2 Hz, (b) shaking involves 15-30° yaw oscillation at 1-2.5 Hz, (c) gestures show smooth sinusoidal profiles with physiologically constrained velocity. The method checks whether detected gestures fall within natural kinematic parameters.

3. **Gesture-Speech Correlation**: Head gestures correlate with speech prosody — nods often coincide with stressed syllables, head movements accompany turn-taking in conversation. The method analyzes temporal correlation between head motion and speech intensity. Deepfakes may show gestures temporally decoupled from speech.

4. **Neck-Head Coordination**: Head rotation involves coupled neck and cervical spine motion with characteristic ranges — large yaw rotations involve torso contribution. The method verifies head-neck-shoulder coordination. Deepfake generators that only manipulate the face may produce head rotations that don't propagate correctly to neck and shoulders.

5. **Inertial Consistency**: Head motion should show proper inertial dynamics — acceleration/deceleration following the mass and muscle force constraints of the head-neck system. The method analyzes the frequency content and jerk profile of head motion. AI-generated head movements may lack natural inertial characteristics.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
